**Instrumentation** (also called **orchestration** or **timbre**) is which instruments and voices you hear and what each
one is doing. Every ▶ on this page plays the instrument named.

## 1. How many performers

| Players | Name |
|---|---|
| 1 | solo |
| 2 | duet (or duo) |
| 3 | trio |
| 4 | quartet |
| 5 | quintet |

A **string quartet** is two violins, a viola and a cello. A **piano trio** is piano, violin and cello. A **choir** is
singers; an **orchestra** is a large group of strings, woodwind, brass and percussion; a **band** usually means a rock,
pop, jazz or wind band.

## 2. Voices

| Voice | Who | Range |
|---|---|---|
| **Soprano** | women, girls | highest |
| **Treble** | boys before their voice changes | high |
| **Alto** (contralto) | women | lower |
| **Countertenor** | men singing in the alto range | alto range |
| **Tenor** | men | high men's voice |
| **Baritone** | men | middle men's voice |
| **Bass** | men | lowest |

An **SATB choir** is soprano, alto, tenor and bass. Sopranos and altos are written in the treble clef; tenors in the treble
clef an octave higher than they sound; basses in the bass clef.

More on voices: [Pop](voice-pop.qmd), [Jazz](voice-jazz.qmd) and [Classical](voice-classical.qmd) singing.

## 3. The orchestra

Four families, each listed from high to low. In a score they are printed in this order, woodwind at the top.

| Family | High → low | How the sound is made |
|---|---|---|
| **Woodwind** | piccolo, flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon | air across a hole (flute) or through a reed |
| **Brass** | trumpet, French horn, trombone, tuba | lips buzzing into a mouthpiece |
| **Percussion** | timpani, snare drum, cymbals, xylophone, glockenspiel… | struck, shaken or scraped |
| **Strings** | violin, viola, cello, double bass | bowed or plucked strings |

## 4. Rock, pop and jazz line-ups

| Group | Usual instruments |
|---|---|
| **Rock / pop band** | lead vocals, electric guitar(s), bass guitar, drum kit, keyboards |
| **Acoustic / folk** | voice, acoustic guitar, maybe fiddle, banjo, mandolin |
| **Jazz combo** | a **rhythm section** (piano or guitar, double bass, drums) and a **front line** (saxophone, trumpet, trombone) |
| **Big band** | saxes, trumpets and trombones in sections, plus the rhythm section |

Gear and how each works: [Guitar](gear-guitar.qmd), [Keyboards](gear-keyboards.qmd), [Drums](gear-drums.qmd),
[Sax](gear-sax.qmd), [Violin](gear-violin.qmd).

## 5. What is each instrument doing?

Naming the instrument is half the answer. Say what it is doing, too:

| Role | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Melody** | the tune |
| **Accompaniment** | the parts that support the tune (chords, rhythm) |
| **Countermelody** | a second tune that fits with the main one |
| **Bass line** | the lowest part |
| **Solo** | one instrument featured, often improvising |

> The melody is on the **violins**, with **cellos** playing a slow bass line and the **horns** holding chords. In the
> second section the melody passes to the **flute**, and the strings change to **pizzicato**.

The techniques that change an instrument's sound (pizzicato, mutes, tremolo, vibrato, falsetto) are in
[Articulation](elements-articulation.qmd#playing-techniques).
